messages:
kevin: raising a high-priority customer escalation from Acme — they reported ~15% 502/504s on /v1/generate around 22:10 UTC, retries are burning their quota. they provided trace id and curl. opening war room now. :rotating_light:

maria: looking at dashboards — ingress p50/p95 climb, backend auth latencies spiked. I see a cluster of timeouts between proxy -> runtime group eu-west-2a. grabbing logs now.

sasha: paste the trace id and the curl they used? I'll check the gateway proxy traces.

kevin: trace id: trace-abc12345. curl they used:
```
curl -v -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED\" -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\n  -d '{"model":"gpt-large","input":"hello"}' \\n  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
They included proxy response headers: `x-request-id: req-9876`, `x-runtime: 504`.

maria: log snippet from runtime ingress at 22:11:
```
[22:11:07] proxy eu-west-2a -> runtime-service: request id=req-9876 status=502 runtime_err=upstream_timeout
[22:11:07] runtime-service eu-west-2a -> model-backend: err=504 seq=2048 backend_latency_ms=1200
```
Looks like the model backend is returning timeouts for long-sequence requests.

dmitri: quick theory — auth cache misses caused authz calls to KMS/token-store which spiked latency and cascaded. I can see a surge of auth-refresh RPCs at the same time. runtime circuit breakers tripped, producing 502s. Also noting heavy request concurrency from this tenant (burst pattern).

ops-bot: Incident created INC-2026-1987 by kevin.

sasha: immediate mitigation suggestions:
- route this tenant to fallback model variant `gpt-large-quantized-standby` in eu to reduce backend work
- lower max_concurrent_requests for /v1/generate route in eu proxy from 200 -> 80
- enable temporary per-tenant rate limit 100r/s and raise retry-backoff recommendations to customer
Anyone can run the routing patch?

maria: I'll apply the routing change and update the proxy config. deploying routing change to eu now, will do rolling restart of proxy nodes (30s windows).

kevin: pinging customer with mitigation plan and asking if they accept fallback + throttling. they accepted. told them we'll follow up with postmortem. :thumbsup:

maria: routing change applied at 22:28 UTC. proxy config diff (applied):
```
- route: tenant-acme -> gpt-large primary
+ route: tenant-acme -> gpt-large-quantized-standby fallback (temporary)
- proxy.max_concurrent_requests: 200
+ proxy.max_concurrent_requests: 80
```
Error rate fell to ~0.6% within 7 minutes. p95 latency normalized.

sasha: good. root-cause candidates and follow-ups:
1) telemetry gap: auth_cache_hit_ratio not emitted at pool-level for runtime groups — we couldn't see auth cache misses early
2) circuit breaker sensitivity for runtime->backend needs tuning for long-seqlen workloads
3) per-tenant default rate limits are too permissive for sudden bursts
4) customer retry guidance: we should enforce default backoff to avoid quota burn

dmitri: action items I'm taking:
- add auth cache exporter from runtime (owner: dmitri)
- tune breaker thresholds and run a short canary with long-sequence synthetic traffic (owner: dmitri)

maria: my action items:
- add alarm for auth RPC p95 > 200ms across runtime groups (owner: maria)
- script the rollback/unset routing to make fallback easy to revert (owner: maria)

kevin: I'll own customer comms and billing check. need to confirm they weren't double-billed for retries and offer credits if appropriate (owner: kevin). scheduled follow-up call tomorrow 15:00 UTC.

sasha: ops follow-up items:
- add circuit-breaker health dashboard and a synthetic probe for eu-west-2a (owner: sasha)
- document 'fallback routing' runbook steps and add to incident playbooks (owner: sasha)

kevin: summary timeline:
- 22:10 incident reported by customer
- 22:14 root cause triage started (auth/cache + runtime timeouts suspected)
- 22:28 routing fallback + proxy limits applied
- 22:35 error rate <1% and customer saw recovery

maria: PM notes: we should also review model backend throttling behavior for long sequences — quantized variant used less memory and reduced backend timeouts.

sasha: long-term follow-ups (owners):
- emit auth_cache metrics at runtime pool granularity (dmitri)
- add alarming and dashboard for runtime circuit-breaker trips (sasha)
- tighten per-tenant rate-limit defaults and expose quick toggle (maria)
- update support playbook to instruct immediate fallback routing for high-error tenant bursts (kevin)

kevin: closing notes: mitigation successful, customer happy with temporary fallback. filing full postmortem and action-items doc. tagging everyone for the async writeup. :white_check_mark:

ops-bot: Incident INC-2026-1987 transitioned to PostmortemPending.
